absent: Locking, sleepability, and interrupt context for page attribute changers and zone init beyond the poking table lock.
Numeric values of page table bits, protection objects, and cache mode encodings.
Implementation of central attribute change, TLB flushing, allocator, paravirtual pinning, and randomness sources.
Layout and flag definitions for executive memory ranges and KASAN shadow interaction.
Runtime use of high memory bounds, persistent map window sizing, and swap limit consumers.
Effects of device tree construction, IOMMU allocation, and firmware table reallocation.
Recovery beyond warning when re encryption or attribute changes fail.

findings.text: Two early boot log helpers report a supplied reason only when the boot processor vulnerability state matches the helper purpose, one for vulnerable processors and one for non vulnerable processors, otherwise remaining silent.

Early initialization establishes a dedicated address space for runtime text patching, selects a randomized base within the unmapped task region when base randomization is enabled while keeping required pages within one middle level span, handles paravirtual pinning and untracked marking, and faults in needed tables ahead of atomic use.

Acquisition of the page table entry for the patching address holds the associated page table lock during lookup and releases it together with unmapping, so table allocation and entry installation are serialized.

Physical page access check returns distinct outcomes for denied system memory, unrestricted access, and low address special handling, consulting overlap with system memory first and then exclusivity of reserved regions, with first megabyte pages receiving exceptional treatment.

Release of an init address interval requires page aligned bounds with warning and normalization on misalignment and no action on empty intervals, then either unmaps the range to trap stray accesses when debug page allocation is active or otherwise removes execute permission, restores writability, and returns pages with poisoning.

Request to mark a page count non executable succeeds trivially on processors lacking the hardware execute disable capability and otherwise applies the attribute through the central page attribute mechanism.
Related helpers adjust writability, presence, and read only state for a page count starting at an address, including a variant that suppresses alias checking to affect only the selected mapping.
Page framed helpers translate a page structure to its kernel address and delegate to the address based read only or writable attribute changers for the requested count.

Freeing a kernel image span delegates to the generic init page release and additionally removes the high kernel alias for the same span when running as 64 bit with page table isolation enabled, while preserving the direct map alias needed to manage freed pages.
Init memory teardown reallocates firmware memory tables, releases unused decrypted memory, and then frees the linker delimited init image span under an identifying label.

Unused decrypted span derived from linker symbols for decrypted storage is re encrypted before release when the memory encryption mask is active, with failure logged and release skipped, otherwise freed as init pages.
Initial ram disk release frees from the given start through the page aligned end, relying on prior reservation of the trailing partial page by early startup and relocation paths.
Zone upper limits are populated from the low memory and total page frame counts with clamping for direct memory access zones and conditional handling for normal and high memory zones.
Per processor 64 bit value holds the mask used to remove tags from translation lookaside buffer state, with one instance per CPU.
Installation of a cache mode for a translation index rejects any non writeback mode at index zero and otherwise updates both directions of the cache to protection translation tables consistently.

Maximum swap file size starts from the generic limit and when the L1 fault bug is present with mitigations enabled is further clamped using a hardware derived page frame limit adjusted for encoded swap offset bits on deeper page table configurations.

Read only after init executive memory descriptor contains five ranges for module text, probes, tracing, packet filter programs, and module data, each recording flags, start, end, protection, and alignment.

Range construction randomizes the common start above the modules base when kernel address randomization is active, selects read only executable protection with cache support when large page support exists, and otherwise falls back to standard kernel protection while always enabling shadow accounting and using a common upper bound.
Executable memory initialization fills a byte range with the architectural trap opcode so stray execution faults.
Two unsigned long globals delimit high memory page frames and a mostly read boolean records whether the virtual allocation start has been established, initially false.

Persistent kernel map table setup has an active early form that initializes a fixed window span and captures its page table pointer and an empty inline form selected for configurations without that window.

Early page table cleanup walks kernel virtual addresses from the low memory limit upward clearing entries for physical memory beyond that limit, warning and aborting if a large mapping is encountered where a single entry was expected, stopping at the first absent level, then proceeding to general paging setup.

Thirty two bit paging bring up initializes permanent tables, flushes translation caches globally, and then builds the device tree for one laptop platform, signalling that early boot allocation is fully available.
Thirty two bit default and supported page entry masks exclude execute disable and global bits, while sixty four bit counterparts permit all bits, with mostly read storage.

High memory sizing accepts a size parameter parsed as bytes shifted to pages, then either trims the low memory limit or adjusts total pages, rejecting oversize values that exceed available pages or leave less than a low memory floor, ignoring requests on kernels without high memory support, and capping non extended builds with diagnostics.

Low memory discovery initializes high memory bounds, derives the high memory pointer from the appropriate page frame limit, associates all memory with one node, marks virtual allocation start as set, and reports low and high memory sizes plus mapped spans.

Supervisor write protection validation maps the zero page read only through a reserved fixmap slot and attempts a faulting store, reporting success and clearing the slot when the store is rejected and otherwise halting boot as unsupported.

Early memory validation allocates input output memory management structures, asserts allocator state on flat memory builds, enforces compile time and runtime ordering among virtual allocation, persistent map, and fixmap regions plus the high memory pointer, then runs the write protection check and marks boot memory as past.

Post init protection write protects early code through constant regions and records completion, with optional debug toggling of the protection, then marks data after text as non executable over a huge page rounded span when hardware supports it.

Sixty four bit table population and entry installation helpers select between safe initialization time variants and normal variants based on a boolean flag, instantiated for each page table level through macro generators.
A global integer records personality flags for thirty two bit execution and a boot option toggles the implied execute behavior according to enable or disable words.
Kernel mapping synchronization for an address interval propagates updates to global page tables.
Helper installs a page entry for a virtual address by indexing the supplied upper directory page and delegating to the low level virtual address setter.

Extra early mappings establish large page kernel entries for a physical span with a chosen cache behavior, requiring large page aligned address and size and empty slots, allocating intermediate tables as needed, exposed as writeback and uncached wrappers.

High kernel mapping cleanup iterates the kernel image window clearing middle level entries outside the text to heap end span, using a hypervisor supplied mapped page count to bound the window when present.

Device memory policy treats the first 256 pages as the low one megabyte special region with distinct return codes, low memory sizing enforces a 64 megabyte floor, and swap sizing accounts for offset encoding width on deeper table levels.

Boot aborts when the dedicated patching address space cannot be allocated or its locked entry cannot be obtained, and when cache mode zero is misprogrammed, while misaligned init spans trigger warning normalization.
